findings.match: ALTER TABLE users RENAME TO users_old;
findings.recommendation: Table renames instantly break any client that has not yet deployed. Create the new table alongside the old one and use an expanding view pattern: expose both names via a VIEW until all clients are migrated, then drop the old name.

Adding NOT NULL without a DEFAULT causes INSERT failures on any client that does not yet supply the new column. Supply a DEFAULT value, or add the column as nullable first, backfill all rows, then add the NOT NULL constraint in a separate migration.

Adding NOT NULL without a DEFAULT causes INSERT failures on any client that does not yet supply the new column. Supply a DEFAULT value, or add the column as nullable first, backfill all rows, then add the NOT NULL constraint in a separate migration.

healing.ddl:
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS users AS
SELECT
    id,
    (first_name || ' ' || last_name) AS name,
    email,
    first_name,
    last_name
FROM users_v2

blast_radius.root_cause: A table was renamed, severing every SQL statement and ORM query that references the original table name. Old application versions continue to issue queries against the now-missing name, causing immediate OperationalErrors at the database layer. Rehearsal confirmed: ✗ Breaking change detected — healing required.

recommended_action: Run `python bifrost.py run --report` in CI to generate the full audit trail (bifrost_audit.json, bifrost.sarif, pr_comment.md, bifrost_remediation.sql).

TABLE RENAME detected: Do not rename the table directly. Instead — (a) create the new table alongside the old one, (b) expose both names via an expanding VIEW until all clients are migrated, (c) then drop the old table in a later release.
NOT NULL WITHOUT DEFAULT detected: Add the column as nullable first, backfill all existing rows, then add the NOT NULL constraint in a separate ALTER TABLE migration.

Apply the generated bifrost_remediation.sql to the production database BEFORE deploying the new application version. This creates the backward-compatible VIEW so legacy queries continue to work during the rolling deployment window.
Once ALL application instances have been updated to reference the new schema directly, drop the compatibility VIEW and remove the remediation patch from your migration history.
Monitor application error rates, slow query logs, and lock-wait metrics for at least 10 minutes after each deployment step.
